passages.text: A song. A Psalm of Asaph.
passages.sermon: This is a song.\r\nThis is a psalm.\r\nAsaph wrote this song and psalm.

passages.text: O God, be not silent; be not speechless; be not still, O God.
passages.sermon:
Asaph wrote this song and psalm.
God, do not be silent.
God, do not be speechless.
God, do not be still.
passages.original: שִׁ֖יר מִזְמ֣וֹר לְאָסָֽף׃ אֱלֹהִ֥ים אַל־ דֳּמִי־ לָ֑ךְ אַל־ תֶּחֱרַ֖שׁ וְאַל־ תִּשְׁקֹ֣ט אֵֽל׃

passages.text: See how Your enemies rage, how Your foes have reared their heads.
passages.sermon:
God has enemies.
God's enemies are angry.
God's enemies make noise.
God has foes.
God's foes lift up their heads.
God's foes act boldly.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ הִנֵּ֣ה א֭וֹיְבֶיךָ יֶהֱמָי֑וּן וּ֝מְשַׂנְאֶ֗יךָ נָ֣שְׂאוּ רֹֽאשׁ׃

passages.text: With cunning they scheme against Your people and conspire against those You cherish, saying, “Come, let us erase them as a nation; may the name of Israel be remembered no more.”
passages.sermon:
God has a people.
God cherishes these people.
Enemies scheme against God's people.
Enemies use cunning plans.
Enemies conspire against those God loves.
Enemies say, “Let us destroy them as a nation.”
Enemies want to erase the name of Israel.
Enemies want no one to remember Israel again.
passages.original: עַֽל־ עַ֭מְּךָ יַעֲרִ֣ימוּ ס֑וֹד וְ֝יִתְיָעֲצ֗וּ עַל־ צְפוּנֶֽיךָ׃ אָמְר֗וּ לְ֭כוּ וְנַכְחִידֵ֣ם מִגּ֑וֹי וְלֹֽא־ יִזָּכֵ֖ר שֵֽׁם־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל עֽוֹד׃

passages.text: For with one mind they plot together, they form an alliance against You— the tents of Edom and the Ishmaelites, of Moab and the Hagrites, of Gebal, Ammon, and Amalek, of Philistia with the people of Tyre.
passages.sermon:
Many nations have become Your enemies.
They have united with one purpose.
They plot together against You, God.
They have formed an alliance against You.
The people of Edom are in this alliance.
The Ishmaelites are also in this alliance.
Moab is part of this group.
The Hagrites have joined them.
Gebal is included among them.
Ammon is part of the alliance.
Amalek is also with them.
Philistia has joined this group.
The people of Tyre are with them too.
passages.original: כִּ֤י נוֹעֲצ֣וּ לֵ֣ב יַחְדָּ֑ו עָ֝לֶ֗יךָ בְּרִ֣ית יִכְרֹֽתוּ׃ אָהֳלֵ֣י אֱ֭דוֹם וְיִשְׁמְעֵאלִ֗ים מוֹאָ֥ב וְהַגְרִֽים׃ גְּבָ֣ל וְ֭עַמּוֹן וַעֲמָלֵ֑ק פְּ֝לֶ֗שֶׁת עִם־ יֹ֥שְׁבֵי צֽוֹר׃

passages.text: Even Assyria has joined them, lending strength to the sons of Lot. Selah Do to them as You did to Midian, as to Sisera and Jabin at the River Kishon, who perished at Endor and became like dung on the ground.
passages.sermon:
Assyria also joined the enemies of Israel.
Assyria gave strength to the sons of Lot.
Selah.
God, act against these enemies as You did against Midian.
Act against them as You did against Sisera and Jabin at the River Kishon.
Sisera and Jabin died at Endor.
They became like dung on the ground.
passages.original: גַּם־ אַ֭שּׁוּר נִלְוָ֣ה עִמָּ֑ם הָ֤י֥וּ זְר֖וֹעַ לִבְנֵי־ ל֣וֹט סֶֽלָה׃ עֲשֵֽׂה־ לָהֶ֥ם כְּמִדְיָ֑ן כְּֽסִֽיסְרָ֥א כְ֝יָבִ֗ין בְּנַ֣חַל קִישֽׁוֹן׃ נִשְׁמְד֥וּ בְֽעֵין־ דֹּ֑אר הָ֥יוּ דֹּ֝֗מֶן לָאֲדָמָֽה׃

passages.text: Make their nobles like Oreb and Zeeb, and all their princes like Zebah and Zalmunna, who said, “Let us possess for ourselves the pastures of God.”
passages.sermon:
God, act against their leaders.
Make their nobles like Oreb and Zeeb.
Make all their princes like Zebah and Zalmunna.
These men said, “Let us take the pastures of God for ourselves.”
passages.original: שִׁיתֵ֣מוֹ נְ֭דִיבֵמוֹ כְּעֹרֵ֣ב וְכִזְאֵ֑ב וּֽכְזֶ֥בַח וּ֝כְצַלְמֻנָּ֗ע כָּל־ נְסִיכֵֽמוֹ׃ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אָ֭מְרוּ נִ֣ירֲשָׁה לָּ֑נוּ אֵ֝֗ת נְא֣וֹת אֱלֹהִֽים׃

passages.text: Make them like tumbleweed, O my God, like chaff before the wind.
passages.sermon:
God, you are powerful.
Make these enemies weak.
Make them like tumbleweed.
Let them be blown away easily.
Make them like chaff.
Let the wind carry them away.
passages.original: אֱ‍ֽלֹהַ֗י שִׁיתֵ֥מוֹ כַגַּלְגַּ֑ל כְּ֝קַ֗שׁ לִפְנֵי־ רֽוּחַ׃

passages.text: As fire consumes a forest, as a flame sets the mountains ablaze, so pursue them with Your tempest, and terrify them with Your storm.
passages.sermon:
Fire burns a forest quickly.
A flame sets mountains on fire.
God, You are powerful.
You can chase Your enemies like a strong wind.
You can frighten them with a violent storm.
passages.original: כְּאֵ֥שׁ תִּבְעַר־ יָ֑עַר וּ֝כְלֶהָבָ֗ה תְּלַהֵ֥ט הָרִֽים׃ כֵּ֭ן תִּרְדְּפֵ֣ם בְּסַעֲרֶ֑ךָ וּבְסוּפָתְךָ֥ תְבַהֲלֵֽם׃

passages.text: Cover their faces with shame, that they may seek Your name, O LORD.
passages.sermon:
This is a prayer to God.
The sons of Korah wrote this psalm.
They ask God to act.
They say, "God, cover their faces with shame."
They want the enemies to feel disgrace.
They want the enemies to seek God's name.
They call God by the name "LORD."
passages.original: מַלֵּ֣א פְנֵיהֶ֣ם קָל֑וֹן וִֽיבַקְשׁ֖וּ שִׁמְךָ֣ יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: May they be ever ashamed and terrified; may they perish in disgrace.
passages.sermon:
They will feel shame forever.
They will feel fear without end.
They will be disgraced.
They will perish.
passages.original: יֵבֹ֖שׁוּ וְיִבָּהֲל֥וּ עֲדֵי־ עַ֗ד וְֽיַחְפְּר֥וּ וְיֹאבֵֽדוּ׃

passages.text: May they know that You alone, whose name is the LORD, are Most High over all the earth.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the Most High over all the earth.
The LORD’s name is above every other name.
The LORD stands alone.
No one else is like the LORD.
Let them know this truth.
passages.original: וְֽיֵדְע֗וּ כִּֽי־ אַתָּ֬ה שִׁמְךָ֣ יְהוָ֣ה לְבַדֶּ֑ךָ עֶ֝לְי֗וֹן עַל־ כָּל־ הָאָֽרֶץ׃
